findings.claim: W-003 on a real share mishandles the very ending it exists to catch. When the hook pressed Stop and the app then reached no stopped ending, Wait-App 600 s kills it, so there is no report. $judged then needs `$null -ne $scan`, so it is false. Get-ShareVerdict returns 'inconclusive' at `if (-not $judged)` before it ever reaches its TIMEOUT -> 'failed' branch. No Check and no Inconclusive() is called on that path, so the case ends 'PASSED: W-003', exit 0, with a record verdict of 'inconclusive'. The contract's FAILED list says 'the app timed out'. Reproduced with Test-W003Real under a stubbed Invoke-WithHook (acted armed line, Exit TIMEOUT, answer 'cut'): it printed verdict=inconclusive with 0 failures.
findings.evidence: Contract 'WindowCases.ps1 -Case W-003 ...': 'FAILED: cutFolderRows is above 0; no timing could be read; a mapping is left; the app timed out.' Get-ShareVerdict (line 7035) checks `-not $judged` before `$exit -ceq 'TIMEOUT'` (7036), and in real mode judged is false whenever the killed app left no report. The main loop (8065-8078) exits 0 when neither Failures nor Inconclusive grew.
findings.fix: In Test-W003Real, after reading $acted and $scan: when the marker was not refused, $acted is not null and $scan is null (or $exit is 'TIMEOUT'), call `Check $false 'Stop was pressed and the app reached no stopped ending within 600 s'`. The failure count then makes Get-ShareVerdict return 'failed' and the case exit 1.

findings.claim: In W-001 -Stopped, a stop attempt that ended abnormally is treated as 'not partial' and retried at half the count. This covers an attempt where the hook pressed Stop during the listing but the app was killed at 3600 s (TIMEOUT), or crashed and left no report. The exit and report checks after the loop look only at the LAST attempt. So Stop hanging a whole-C:\ scan for an hour, followed by a clean partial retry, writes stopped.verdict 'held' and the case passes. The timeout is visible only as attempts=2 and a console line. The contract says a stopped run that timed out is FAILED. Reproduced with Invoke-W001StoppedRun under a stubbed Invoke-HookedRun (attempt 1: acted line with sized '-', Exit TIMEOUT, no report; attempt 2: Cancelled and partial): it printed stopped verdict=held with 0 failures.
findings.evidence: Contract 'WindowCases.ps1 -Case W-001': 'FAILED (exit 1): ... the stopped run is aborted, or notInFinished or codeChanged is above 0, or it timed out or threw: stopped.verdict 'failed', written in a finally.' The retry rule in the design is for a run that ended normally but was not partial (Completed, or stopped while sizing). The function's own header says 'with verdict 'failed' when the run threw or timed out'.
findings.fix: Inside the attempt loop, right after Invoke-HookedRun, `if ($run.Exit -cne '0' -or $null -eq $run.Report) { break }`. Only a run that ended with a report and exit 0 but was not partial is retried. The CheckEqual and Check after the loop then fail on the abnormal attempt, and the stopped verdict is 'failed'.

findings.claim: In W-003 real mode, a marker the hook refused (its fixed 60 s deadline was missed) is only echoed with Write-Output. Neither Inconclusive() nor Check is called, and with $refused true the other two Inconclusive branches are skipped. So the case ends 'PASSED: W-003', exit 0, for a run where nothing was pressed. Only the record says 'inconclusive'. O-003 decided this ending is INCONCLUSIVE, even when Wait-App later reports TIMEOUT. Reproduced: with a refused line in the hook log and Exit TIMEOUT, it printed failures=0 inconclusive=False.
findings.evidence: O-003 (discharged): 'If the hook log has its marker refusal line, the verdict is INCONCLUSIVE, even when Wait-App later reports TIMEOUT.' Contract: 'INCONCLUSIVE: ... an answer other than 'cut', or the marker refused after the hook's 60 s deadline'. Main loop: exit 3 only when $script:Inconclusive grew.
findings.fix: Replace the Write-Output at line 7152 with `Inconclusive 'W-003: the hook''s 60 s marker deadline was missed ...'`, keeping the same wording.

quote.text: if ($refused) { Write-Output '        The hook''s 60 s marker deadline was missed: the cut and the typed cut did not both land within 60 s of the launch. Nothing was pressed.' }

findings.claim: Test-W001 starts the -Stopped run whenever the finished run wrote a report, whatever its status. A finished run that ended RootUnreadable, Refused or Cancelled therefore still costs the maintainer a second whole-C:\ scan, with kernel pool possibly held until a restart. It also writes a 'stopped' part compared against a tab that was never a finished one. The design says the stopped run happens only after a Completed finished run, and that otherwise no stopped part is written. Reproduced: with a finished report of status RootUnreadable and -Stopped, Invoke-W001StoppedRun was called.
findings.evidence: Design component 'W-001 -Stopped': 'This runs only after the finished run has a report with status Completed. Otherwise the case is already FAILED, and no stopped part is written.' Line 6770 only CheckEquals the status and carries on.
findings.fix: `if ($Stopped -and [string]$run.Report.core.status -ceq 'Completed') { Invoke-W001StoppedRun ... } elseif ($Stopped) { Write-Output '        no stopped run: the finished run did not end Completed' }`.

findings.claim: Test-W002 runs `CheckEqual 'Completed' $scan.core.status` unconditionally. A scan that ended Refused, RootUnreadable or Cancelled is therefore a FAILURE (exit 1), while Get-HydrationVerdict writes 'inconclusive' into the record and Inconclusive() is also called. The console and the committed record disagree, and the case's ending contradicts decision n1 ('INCONCLUSIVE when core.status is not Completed'). Reproduced: with -Root on a temp folder and a stubbed app that wrote status Refused, it printed failures=1, verdict=inconclusive.
findings.evidence: Decision n1 (accepted, O-039): 'the builder makes W-002 FAILED on a non-zero exit or a missing report, and INCONCLUSIVE when core.status is not 'Completed''. The contract's W-002 FAILED list does not include a status that is not Completed.
findings.fix: Delete the CheckEqual on line 6979. Get-HydrationVerdict's 'inconclusive' and the Inconclusive line at 6983 already report that status, and exit and report presence keep their Checks at 6977-6978.

findings.claim: Invoke-W001StoppedRun retries any attempt that is not partial, including one that ended TIMEOUT (the hook pressed Stop and the app never reached its ending within 3600 s), one that exited non-zero, and one that left no report. Only the last attempt's $run.Exit and $run.Report are checked (CheckEqual '0' $run.Exit). So a Stop that hung the app on the maintainer's whole-C:\ run is retried at half the folder count, and if that retry is clean the stopped part is written with verdict 'held'. The design's error_cases say the stopped run 'timed out or threw: stopped.verdict failed'. Reproduced with Invoke-HookedRun stubbed: attempt 1 returned TIMEOUT with no report after an 'acted mode=stop ... sized=-' line, attempt 2 was a clean Cancelled run, and the result was attempts=2, verdict=held, failures=0. The console only says 'stopped run 1 was not partial (status , sized <null>)'.
findings.evidence: tests/window/WindowCases.ps1:6650-6664. The loop condition is '-not $partial' only. Test-StoppedPartial is false for a null status, so a TIMEOUT attempt is halved and retried. CheckEqual '0' $run.Exit at 6664 sees only the final attempt. Design contract 'WindowCases.ps1 -Case W-001 ... -Stopped': FAILED when 'the stopped run is aborted, ... or it timed out or threw'.
findings.fix: Stop retrying, and fail, when an attempt ends with Exit other than '0' or with no report. Retry only when the app exited 0 with a report and the run was not partial (Completed, sized not '-', or no acted line). For example, inside the loop: if ($run.Exit -cne '0' -or $null -eq $run.Report) { Check $false "stopped run ${attempt}: the app ended $($run.Exit) with no stopped ending"; break }. The existing failure mark then makes the verdict 'failed'.

findings.claim: Get-W001RootShape classes -Root by its text, and the app classes it after LongPath.NormalizeRoot. 'C:/', 'C:\\' and 'C:\.' are classed 'folder' and '\\?\C:\' is classed 'unc', yet the app scans every one of them as the whole C:\ (GetFullPath folds the first three to 'C:\', and the extended prefix is stripped). On such a root, W-001 runs an hour-long whole-C:\ scan and then silently skips the local-letter-only checks: outcome completed, coverage present, panel on screen, and reason/code mismatches. It writes the record to artifacts/w001-run.json, not docs/proof-runs/w001-c-drive.json, and the -Force/stopped-part guard looks at the wrong file. For 'C:/' and 'C:\.', $wholeDrive is false as well, so the wcifs-layer-store precaution check is also skipped. Get-ProofRecordPath takes the letter from $root.Substring(0,1), which is '\' for '\\?\C:\'. Measured with the real functions: 'C:/' gives folder and artifacts\w001-run.json, 'C:\\' gives folder, 'C:\.' gives folder, '\\?\C:\' gives unc.
findings.evidence: tests/window/WindowCases.ps1:6410 '^[A-Za-z]:\\?$' is the only letter test, and 6414 treats any '^\\\\' root whose GetPathRoot is itself as 'unc'. src/FsAnalyser.Core/Native/LongPath.cs:27-41: an extended root is stripped to its display form, and any other root goes through Path.GetFullPath. Lesson #13 asks for an enumeration of root spellings.
findings.fix: Normalise the root before classifying it. In Get-W001RootShape (and for the letter in Get-ProofRecordPath), strip a leading '\\?\' or '\\.\' when it is followed by a drive letter, run a non-UNC rooted path through [System.IO.Path]::GetFullPath, and match the letter regex on the result. Alternatively, refuse any spelling that is not 'X:' or 'X:\' with a throw before scanning. Test-W001 should also pass the same normalised root to $wholeDrive and Get-ProofRecordPath.
findings.class_of: root spellings the proof cases take as typed rather than as the app normalises them

findings.claim: Seam.ListFiles builds its search path as Extended(root.TrimEnd('\\')) + "\\*", which puts a \\?\ prefix on the root as typed, and \\?\ paths are not normalised. For a root with forward slashes, or one ending '\.', the first FindFirstFileExW fails and the listing comes back empty, yet the app scans that folder normally (GetFullPath). W-002 then reports 0 files before and after and ends INCONCLUSIVE ('0 files online-only before') after the scan, with nothing saying the lister read nothing. On the maintainer's OneDrive that is a wasted proof run. Measured: on one temp tree, plain root 2 files, '/' root 0, trailing '\.' 0.
findings.evidence: tests/window/WindowCases.ps1:5542 pending.Push(root.TrimEnd('\\')) and 5547 FindFirstFileEx(Extended(folder) + "\\*", ...). Test-W002 passes $Root straight through, at 6956 ($sync = $Root) and 6960. Same family as m1.
findings.fix: In ListFiles, unless the root already starts with \\?\, normalise it with Path.GetFullPath before Extended (for example root = root.StartsWith(@"\\?\") ? root : Path.GetFullPath(root)). Or have Test-W002 pass [System.IO.Path]::GetFullPath($Root) to both the lister and the app.
findings.class_of: root spellings the proof cases take as typed rather than as the app normalises them

findings.claim: Test-W003Real waits for the typed 'cut' with $typed = [Console]::In.ReadLineAsync() and then loops while -not $typed.IsCompleted, printing seconds since launch. Console.In is a synchronized TextReader, and its ReadLineAsync runs ReadLine synchronously, so the call does not return until a line arrives. Measured in a child pwsh with stdin held open: the call returned after 3825 ms, with IsCompleted already True. As a result the seconds-since-launch counter never shows while the person makes the cut. O-003's decided step 2 is that the console 'shows the seconds elapsed since launch', against the hook's fixed 60 s MarkerDeadline. The -not $process.HasExited exit from the wait is dead too, so a scan that ends first still waits for Enter.
findings.evidence: tests/window/WindowCases.ps1:7139-7145. Measured with ProcessStartInfo('pwsh', '-Command $t=[Console]::In.ReadLineAsync(); ...'), writing a line after 4 s: 'returned after 3825 ms, IsCompleted=True, result=cut'. O-003 discharge text, item 2.
findings.fix: Poll for input instead of calling ReadLineAsync: loop on [Console]::KeyAvailable (an interactive console) and read with [Console]::ReadKey, building up the line, while printing the counter and checking $process.HasExited. Or run the ReadLine on a separate runspace or thread job, so that the loop really runs while the read is pending.

findings.claim: Get-OracleRow classes a code-5 row whose plain open now fails with any error other than 0, 2, 3 or 5 as 'refused-another-code', which fails W-001 through Get-LeakCount. The class's own rationale is that access is checked before sharing, so a 32 means the ACL let the plain open through. That rationale does not hold for errors that arise before any access check: network errors (53, 59, 64, 67, 121, 1231) from a share whose server dropped after the scan, and device errors (21, 1167). For those, the attribute-only Times open fails as well, so the changed-since-scan exemption cannot apply. A W-001 on a network letter or UNC root (Z:\ here is intermittently down, per lesson #878) then reports a false C4 failure: 'its code would be another call's'.
findings.evidence: tests/window/WindowCases.ps1:6346-6350. `if ($probe.Error -ne 0) { $times = ...Times(...); if ($times.TimesRead -and ...) { return 'changed-since-scan' }; return 'refused-another-code' }`. Get-LeakCount at 6384 adds the class to the leaks, and it applies to every root shape (declared deviation).
findings.fix: Return 'refused-another-code' only for errors that come after the access check (32, 33, and any others shown to come after it). Class network and device errors, for example the UnreadableRows.PlainPhrase network family together with 21 and 1167, as 'other-code' or 'gone-since-scan', which are tallied and never failed.
